## What composition looks like

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```julia
using ComposableTuringIDModels, Distributions, Turing, Accessors

ar2 = AR(;
  damp = [truncated(Normal(0.2, 0.2), 0, 1),
          truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0, 1)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1)))
ma1 = MA(;
  θ = [truncated(Normal(0.0, 0.2), -1, 1)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1)))

arma21 = @set ar2.ϵ_t = ma1
arima211 = DiffLatentModel(arma21, Normal(0, 0.2); d = 1)

mdl = IDModel(
  DirectInfections(; Z = arima211, initialisation = Normal()),
  PoissonError())
chain = sample(as_turing_model(mdl, cases, n), NUTS(), 1_000)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## The prototype is `ComposableTuringIDModels.jl`
A proof of concept rather than a finished package. Registered in
General at v0.1.1, so `] add ComposableTuringIDModels` works ·
[github.com/EpiAware/ComposableTuringIDModels.jl][ctim]
:::
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
![](../figures/composable-arima.png){height="500px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="MA(1) inside AR(2) inside ARMA inside ARIMA, then Poisson"}

::: {.callout-note}
`@set` is Accessors.jl, not ours. It works because the components are
plain immutable structs. `AR` was never told that `MA` exists.
:::

::: {.attribution}
Keywords track `main`. The paper's artefact pins an earlier release,
where these were `damp_priors`, `θ_priors` and `std_prior` ·
[doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675)
:::
:::

## Reusing that AR(2) for South Korea

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The first replication takes the AR(2) from the worked example, a
  renewal process with a discretised serial interval, and a negative
  binomial observation model
- **A** to **C** are prior predictive checks on each part, **D**
  compares the continuous serial interval with its discretised form
- **E** and **F** recover the paper's finding. $R_t$ in South Korea
  peaked near 10 and dropped below 1 in early March 2020

::: {.attribution}
Replicating [Mishra et al. (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16487).
Figure from the paper
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/composable-mishra.png){width="88%" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Six panels: prior checks on each part, then the joint fit"}
:::
::::

## A common `EpiNow2` configuration, rebuilt out of parts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- An ARIMA(2,1,1) latent process and a negative binomial observation
  model, both lifted unchanged from the worked example and the South
  Korea replication
- `broadcast_weekly` for weekly $R_t$, day-of-week ascertainment around
  the observation model, and two `LatentDelay` wrappers for the
  incubation period and the reporting delay
- **A** to **D** validate each part on its own. **E** and **F** are the
  joint fit, recovering cases through the delays and $R_t$ with them

::: {.callout-important}
No component was edited and no new component code was written.
:::

::: {.attribution}
Structure is the `EpiNow2` panel of Figure 2, results Figure 4. Daily
COVID-19 cases from Italy, February to June 2020, shipped with
`EpiNow2`. Replicating
[EpiNow2](https://doi.org/10.12688/wellcomeopenres.16006.2)
(Abbott et al., 2020),
[Mishra et al. (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16487) and
[Chatzilena et al. (2019)][chatzilena].
One configuration replicated, not a benchmark against the package
:::
:::

## Swap the infection process, keep everything downstream

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The third replication drops the renewal process and uses an SIR model
  built with `ODEProcess` over the SciML solvers instead
- Everything downstream is unchanged. A Poisson observation model, and
  a second version wrapping it in `Ascertainment` driven by an AR(1)
- **C** shows both landing on the same posterior $R_0$, tight and well
  away from the prior. **E** and **F** show the deterministic fit is
  the worse calibrated of the two

::: {.callout-important}
The infection process changed and nothing downstream had to.
:::

::: {.attribution}
Replicating Chatzilena et al. (2019),
[doi:10.1016/j.epidem.2019.100367][chatzilena]. An influenza outbreak
in an English boarding school, 1978. Figure 5 of the paper,
[doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675).
The paper's text reads $R_0 \approx 2$ off this panel. Panel C looks
closer to 4 to me, and I have not resolved which is right
:::
:::
